proof.text: For every $i$, the inclusions of subcomplexes give quotient complexes $P_{i+1}/P_i$ and $Q_{i+1}/Q_i$. Because each inclusion is split on the underlying graded abelian groups, the rows $0\to P_i\to P_{i+1}\to P_{i+1}/P_i\to0$ and $0\to Q_i\to Q_{i+1}\to Q_{i+1}/Q_i\to0$ are degreewise split exact. The condition $f(P_i)\subseteq Q_i$ makes $f$ a morphism between these short exact rows, with third component the induced quotient map.

proof.text: Apply the long exact cohomology sequence and its naturality to the two rows from Step 1. For each cohomological degree $n$, use the five consecutive terms $H^{n-1}(P_{i+1}/P_i)\to H^n(P_i)\to H^n(P_{i+1})\to H^n(P_{i+1}/P_i)\to H^{n+1}(P_i)$ and the corresponding $Q$ terms. The quotient map is a quasi-isomorphism by hypothesis. Starting with $P_0=Q_0=0$, induction on $i$ and the five lemma show that $H^n(P_i)\to H^n(Q_i)$ is an isomorphism for every $i,n$: the four arrows surrounding the middle one are isomorphisms by the induction hypothesis and the quotient quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: agent-written auxiliary to lem-coef-dg-module-base-change steps 6 and 10: induction over finite stages by the long exact sequence and five lemma

proof.text: The unions are directed unions of subgroups in every degree. Therefore cycles and boundaries satisfy $Z^n(P)=\bigcup_i Z^n(P_i)$ and $B^n(P)=\bigcup_i B^n(P_i)$, and similarly for $Q$: a cycle or a boundary witness involves finitely many elements and hence lies in one stage. It follows directly that $\varinjlim_i H^n(P_i)\to H^n(P)$ and $\varinjlim_i H^n(Q_i)\to H^n(Q)$ are bijections: representatives, equalities, and a null-homology witness can all be moved to a common later stage. The isomorphisms from Step 2 thus induce an isomorphism $H^n(f):H^n(P)\to H^n(Q)$ for every $n$, so $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: For dg modules, evaluate the filtrations and the map at each object of the small dg category. The hypotheses remain exactly those of the complex argument: the evaluated filtrations are exhaustive, graded-split filtrations by subcomplexes compatible with the evaluated map, and each quotient map is a quasi-isomorphism. Steps 1–3 therefore give a quasi-isomorphism at every object, which is precisely an objectwise quasi-isomorphism of dg modules.

title: Quasi-isomorphism from exhaustive filtered graded pieces
statement: Use the cochain-complex and quasi-isomorphism conventions of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. Let $f:P\to Q$ be a chain map of cochain complexes of abelian groups, and let $0=P_0\subset P_1\subset\cdots$ and $0=Q_0\subset Q_1\subset\cdots$ be increasing sequences of subcomplexes with $f(P_i)\subseteq Q_i$ for every $i$, each inclusion split on the underlying graded abelian groups, and with $P=\bigcup_iP_i$ and $Q=\bigcup_iQ_i$. If every induced map on successive quotient complexes $P_{i+1}/P_i\to Q_{i+1}/Q_i$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently, use right dg modules over a small dg category, dg submodules and objectwise quasi-isomorphisms as in [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement] (covariant dg modules over $\mathcal C$ being right dg modules over $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$): for a map $f:P\to Q$ of such dg modules with increasing filtrations by dg submodules $0=P_0\subset P_1\subset\cdots$, $0=Q_0\subset Q_1\subset\cdots$ satisfying, at every object, all the hypotheses above (compatibility with $f$, graded splitting, exhaustiveness), and whose successive quotient maps are objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, $f$ is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism.

Step 3 (Z^n and B^n of a directed union are the unions, so cohomology commutes with the union) and step 4 (evaluation at each object) are genuinely elementary. The statement matches its only citer, lem-coef-dg-module-base-change, at steps 6 and 10.
